# umami Provider

The Umami provider manages websites, teams, team members, share links, tracked links, pixels and users in [Umami](https://umami.is/), self-hosted or Umami Cloud.

## Authentication

Use an API key (Umami v3.4.0+ or Umami Cloud), created under Settings → API keys. On older self-hosted instances, use the username and password of a user without two-factor authentication. Use a dedicated non-admin user: admin credentials can read and delete every website on the instance. Only `umami_user` needs an admin, and Umami refuses API keys for it, so configure a second provider with an admin `username` and `password` and an `alias` for those resources (see the `umami_user` example).

## Example Usage

```terraform
provider "umami" {
  endpoint = "https://stats.example.com/api" # Also configurable via UMAMI_API_CLIENT_ENDPOINT
  api_key  = var.umami_api_key               # Also configurable via UMAMI_API_KEY

  # On instances older than v3.4.0, log in instead (the user must not have 2FA):
  # username = "automation" # Also configurable via UMAMI_USERNAME
  # password = "..."        # Also configurable via UMAMI_PASSWORD
}

variable "umami_api_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `api_key` (String, Sensitive) Umami API key (`umami_...`), created under Settings → API keys. Also set by `UMAMI_API_KEY`.
- `endpoint` (String) Umami API base URL, including the API path: `https://<your-umami>/api` when self-hosted, or `https://api.umami.is/v1` for Umami Cloud. Also set by `UMAMI_API_CLIENT_ENDPOINT`.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Password to log in with. Also set by `UMAMI_PASSWORD`.
- `username` (String) Username to log in with, for self-hosted instances. The user must not have two-factor authentication enabled. Also set by `UMAMI_USERNAME`.
